current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh direct address opens this unit, כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.46.19, byte), matching “You daughter who dwells in Egypt, furnish yourself to go into captivity; for Memphis will become a desolation, and will be burned up, without inhabitant.” (web:Jer.46.19) — יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, addressed directly to Egypt personified as a dwelling daughter, distinct from the oath just closed. A setumah stands at the close of oshb:Jer.46.19 in the paragraph-mark inventory (single-witness WLC evidence, weak corroboration in the Prophets). The heifer simile follows, עֶגְלָ֥ה יְפֵֽה פִיָּ֖ה מִצְרָ֑יִם קֶ֥רֶץ מִצָּפ֖וֹן בָּ֥א בָֽא (oshb:Jer.46.20, byte), matching “Egypt is a very beautiful heifer; but destruction out of the north has come. It has come.” (web:Jer.46.20), continuing in the third person through the hired men's own flight, גַּם שְׂכִרֶ֤יהָ בְקִרְבָּהּ֙ כְּעֶגְלֵ֣י מַרְבֵּ֔ק כִּֽי גַם הֵ֧מָּה הִפְנ֛וּ נָ֥סוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו לֹ֣א עָמָ֑דוּ כִּ֣י י֥וֹם אֵידָ֛ם בָּ֥א עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם (oshb:Jer.46.21, byte), matching “Also her hired men in the middle of her are like calves of the stall, for they also are turned back. They have fled away together. They didn’t stand, for the day of their calamity has come on them, the time of their visitation.” (web:Jer.46.21), the advancing army's sound, קוֹלָ֖הּ כַּנָּחָ֣שׁ יֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי בְחַ֣יִל יֵלֵ֔כוּ וּבְקַרְדֻּמּוֹת֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔הּ כְּחֹטְבֵ֖י עֵצִֽים (oshb:Jer.46.22, byte), matching “Its sound will go like the serpent, for they will march with an army, and come against her with axes, as wood cutters.” (web:Jer.46.22), and the felling of her forest, כָּרְת֤וּ יַעְרָהּ֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֖י לֹ֣א יֵֽחָקֵ֑ר כִּ֤י רַבּוּ֙ מֵֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מִסְפָּֽר (oshb:Jer.46.23, byte), matching “They will cut down her forest," says Yahweh, "though it can’t be searched; because they are more than the locusts, and are innumerable.” (web:Jer.46.23) — the neum-YHWH here sits mid-verse, before the locust comparison that completes the sentence, not as a closing tag. The unit closes on the third-person return of the construct that opened it in second-person address, הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד עַם צָפֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.46.24, byte), matching “The daughter of Egypt will be disappointed; she will be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.” (web:Jer.46.24) — the bat-Mitsrayim construct itself, standing at three verses book-wide at the skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier: oshb:Jer.46.11, oshb:Jer.46.19, oshb:Jer.46.24), brackets the span; the opening edge at oshb:Jer.46.19 is a second-person address, while this closing edge is third-person throughout, so the bracket is on the recurring figure rather than on the address, and the same construct also stands outside this span at oshb:Jer.46.11, בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת מִצְרָ֑יִם, under the same second-person address that opens this unit; oshb:Jer.46.11 itself carries a ketiv/qere pair elsewhere in the verse (single-witness), not touching the quoted phrase. A differently-framed divine pronouncement opens the next verse, אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֤י פוֹקֵד֙ אֶל אָמ֣וֹן מִנֹּ֔א וְעַל פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל מִצְרַ֔יִם וְעַל אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ וְעַל מְלָכֶ֑יהָ וְעַ֨ל פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְעַ֥ל הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בּֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.46.25, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Behold, I will punish Amon of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with her gods and her kings, even Pharaoh, and those who trust in him.” (web:Jer.46.25), and this row does not reach it.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A setumah closes oshb:Jer.46.26 in the parashah inventory (WLC, single-witness; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own opening address to Jacob, distinct in both addressee and content from the judgment just closed, וְ֠אַתָּה אַל תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ וְאַל תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲק֛וֹב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד (oshb:Jer.46.27, byte), matching “But don’t you be afraid, Jacob my servant. Don’t be dismayed, Israel; for, behold, I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and will be quiet and at ease. No one will make him afraid.” (web:Jer.46.27) — Yahweh's servant Jacob is comforted with a promise of return from the very captivity just pronounced on Egypt's own gods and king. oshb:Jer.46.27 itself carries a closing setumah in the marked-verse layer (WLC-sourced, single witness only, weak in the Prophets by owner ruling). The comfort is repeated and sharpened in the verse that follows, אַ֠תָּה אַל תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אִתְּךָ֖ אָ֑נִי כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִדַּחְתִּ֣יךָ שָׁ֗מָּה וְאֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹא אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.46.28, byte), matching “Don’t be afraid, O Jacob my servant,” says Yahweh, “for I am with you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you, but I will not make a full end of you, but I will correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.” (web:Jer.46.28) — the four-token address run אַל תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ stands byte-identical at oshb:Jer.46.27 and oshb:Jer.46.28, diverging only in the conjunction on the opening word, וְ֠אַתָּה at oshb:Jer.46.27 against אַ֠תָּה at oshb:Jer.46.28, before this verse turns to its own distinction, that the nations will meet a full end while Jacob will not; this verse itself carries a paseq (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). The parashah inventory marks oshb:Jer.46.28 with a setumah (WLC single witness; the Prophets addendum holds this tier-3 and never a driver). That second mark ends both this row and the whole of chapter 46. The next chapter opens on a fresh nations-header for a different people, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכֶּ֥ה פַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת עַזָּֽה (oshb:Jer.47.1, byte), matching “Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.” (web:Jer.47.1), and this row does not reach it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this couplet under the same label as the rest of the Egypt header material was considered; it is set aside because the addressee, content, and outcome (comfort and return rather than judgment) reverse those of the surrounding material, and the controlled vocabulary's salvation_oracle value names exactly this kind of passage outside its own core chapters.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A setumah stands at the close of oshb:Jer.46.28 in the paragraph-mark inventory (single-witness WLC evidence, weak corroboration in the Prophets). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own fresh nations-header, אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא אֶל פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים בְּטֶ֛רֶם יַכֶּ֥ה פַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת עַזָּֽה (oshb:Jer.47.1, byte), matching “Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.” (web:Jer.47.1) — the asher-hayah debar-YHWH el-Yirmeyahu shape again, one of the same four sites already cited for the rubric opening this nations collection, here dated by a temporal clause on בְּטֶ֛רֶם (beterem) plus a prefix-conjugation verb rather than a numbered year, the note that it comes before Pharaoh struck Gaza. oshb:Jer.47.1 carries its own setumah in the parashah layer, disclosed as WLC single-witness texture, tier-3 weak among the Prophets. That mark does not by itself drive a cut here, since the divine-speech formula that follows only sets this unit's frame rather than changing an already-established one. That formula opens the flood vision directly, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנֵּה מַ֜יִם עֹלִ֤ים מִצָּפוֹן֙ וְהָיוּ֙ לְנַ֣חַל שׁוֹטֵ֔ף וְיִשְׁטְפוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ וּמְלוֹאָ֔הּ עִ֖יר וְיֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ וְזָֽעֲקוּ֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם וְהֵילִ֕ל כֹּ֖ל יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Jer.47.2, byte), matching “Yahweh says: "Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and will become an overflowing stream, and will overflow the land and all that is therein, the city and those who dwell therein. The men will cry, and all the inhabitants of the land will wail.” (web:Jer.47.2) — this verse itself carries a paseq (single-witness, seg layer, count-only). The vision continues without a break, מִקּ֗וֹל שַֽׁעֲטַת֙ פַּרְס֣וֹת אַבִּירָ֔יו מֵרַ֣עַשׁ לְרִכְבּ֔וֹ הֲמ֖וֹן גַּלְגִּלָּ֑יו לֹֽא הִפְנ֤וּ אָבוֹת֙ אֶל בָּנִ֔ים מֵֽרִפְי֖וֹן יָדָֽיִם (oshb:Jer.47.3, byte), matching “At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong ones, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers don’t look back for their children because their hands are so feeble,” (web:Jer.47.3), naming the day's purpose, עַל הַיּ֗וֹם הַבָּא֙ לִשְׁד֣וֹד אֶת כָּל פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים לְהַכְרִ֤ית לְצֹר֙ וּלְצִיד֔וֹן כֹּ֖ל שָׂרִ֣יד עֹזֵ֑ר כִּֽי שֹׁדֵ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים שְׁאֵרִ֖ית אִ֥י כַפְתּֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.47.4, byte), matching “because of the day that comes to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every helper who remains; for Yahweh will destroy the Philistines, the remnant of the isle of Caphtor.” (web:Jer.47.4), and closing on the panic in Gaza and Ashkelon, בָּ֤אָה קָרְחָה֙ אֶל עַזָּ֔ה נִדְמְתָ֥ה אַשְׁקְל֖וֹן שְׁאֵרִ֣ית עִמְקָ֑ם עַד מָתַ֖י תִּתְגּוֹדָֽדִי (oshb:Jer.47.5, byte), matching “Baldness has come on Gaza; Ashkelon is brought to nothing. You remnant of their valley, how long will you cut yourself?” (web:Jer.47.5). A setumah closes oshb:Jer.47.5 in the parashah inventory (WLC, single-witness; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum). That second mark corroborates the row's own close immediately before the sword-apostrophe that opens the next verse, ה֗וֹי חֶ֚רֶב לַֽיהוָ֔ה עַד אָ֖נָה לֹ֣א תִשְׁקֹ֑טִי הֵאָֽסְפִי֙ אַל תַּעְרֵ֔ךְ הֵרָגְעִ֖י וָדֹֽמִּי (oshb:Jer.47.6, byte), matching “‘You sword of Yahweh, how long will it be before you are quiet? Put yourself back into your scabbard; rest, and be still.’” (web:Jer.47.6).

current_row.boundary_rationale: oshb:Jer.47.5 itself carries a closing setumah in the marked-verse layer (WLC-sourced, single witness only, weak in the Prophets by owner ruling). That mark falls immediately before this unit's own hoy onset, distinct from the vision just closed, ה֗וֹי חֶ֚רֶב לַֽיהוָ֔ה עַד אָ֖נָה לֹ֣א תִשְׁקֹ֑טִי הֵאָֽסְפִי֙ אַל תַּעְרֵ֔ךְ הֵרָגְעִ֖י וָדֹֽמִּי (oshb:Jer.47.6, byte), matching “‘You sword of Yahweh, how long will it be before you are quiet? Put yourself back into your scabbard; rest, and be still.’” (web:Jer.47.6) — this is the sword-apostrophe class, the prophet's own address to Yahweh's sword rather than to any human or national addressee. The apostrophe is answered in the verse that follows it without a further break, אֵ֣יךְ תִּשְׁקֹ֔טִי וַֽיהוָ֖ה צִוָּה לָ֑הּ אֶֽל אַשְׁקְל֛וֹן וְאֶל ח֥וֹף הַיָּ֖ם שָׁ֥ם יְעָדָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.47.7, byte), matching “How can you be quiet, since Yahweh has given you a command? Against Ashkelon, and against the seashore, there he has appointed it.” (web:Jer.47.7), closing the whole Philistine oracle on the sword's own divine commission against Ashkelon and the seashore. Ask him who flees, and her who escapes; say, ‘What has been done?’” (web:Jer.48.19) — the inhabitant of Aroer. The summons closes on a general proclamation, הֹבִ֥ישׁ מוֹאָ֛ב כִּֽי חַ֖תָּה הילילי הֵילִ֣ילוּ וזעקי וּֽזְעָ֑קוּ הַגִּ֣ידוּ בְאַרְנ֔וֹן כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מוֹאָֽב (oshb:Jer.48.20, byte), matching “Moab is disappointed; for it is broken down. A differently-formed unit opens the next verse — a bare list of place names rather than a further direct address — וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט בָּ֖א אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ הַמִּישֹׁ֑ר אֶל חֹל֥וֹן וְאֶל יַ֖הְצָה וְעַל מופעת מֵיפָֽעַת (oshb:Jer.48.21, byte), matching “Judgment has come on the plain country— on Holon, on Jahzah, on Mephaath,” (web:Jer.48.21), and this row does not reach it.

A fresh communal voice opens the next verse, reporting rather than commanding, שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן מוֹאָ֖ב גֵּאֶ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד גָּבְה֧וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ וְגַאֲוָת֖וֹ וְרֻ֥ם לִבּֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.48.29, byte), matching “We have heard of the pride of Moab. They will mourn for the men of Kir Heres.” (web:Jer.48.31), turning to direct address of a vineyard, מִבְּכִ֨י יַעְזֵ֤ר אֶבְכֶּה לָּךְ֙ הַגֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה נְטִֽישֹׁתַ֨יִךְ֙ עָ֣בְרוּ יָ֔ם עַ֛ד יָ֥ם יַעְזֵ֖ר נָגָ֑עוּ עַל קֵיצֵ֥ךְ וְעַל בְּצִירֵ֖ךְ שֹׁדֵ֥ד נָפָֽל (oshb:Jer.48.32, byte), matching “With more than the weeping of Jazer I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches passed over the sea. They reached even to the sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your summer fruits and on your vintage.” (web:Jer.48.32) — the vine of Sibmah is addressed directly, held inside the same continuing lament voice rather than a fresh scene of its own. The weeping continues, וְנֶאֶסְפָ֨ה שִׂמְחָ֥ה וָגִ֛יל מִכַּרְמֶ֖ל וּמֵאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֑ב וְיַ֨יִן֙ מִיקָבִ֣ים הִשְׁבַּ֔תִּי לֹֽא יִדְרֹ֣ךְ הֵידָ֔ד הֵידָ֖ד לֹ֥א הֵידָֽד (oshb:Jer.48.33, byte), matching “Gladness and joy is taken away from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab. I have caused wine to cease from the wine presses. No one will tread with shouting. The shouting will be no shouting.” (web:Jer.48.33), widening into a geography of cries, מִזַּעֲקַ֨ת חֶשְׁבּ֜וֹן עַד אֶלְעָלֵ֗ה עַד יַ֨הַץ֙ נָתְנ֣וּ קוֹלָ֔ם מִצֹּ֨עַר֙ עַד חֹ֣רֹנַ֔יִם עֶגְלַ֖ת שְׁלִֽשִׁיָּ֑ה כִּ֚י גַּם מֵ֣י נִמְרִ֔ים לִמְשַׁמּ֖וֹת יִהְיֽוּ (oshb:Jer.48.34, byte), matching “From the cry of Heshbon even to Elealeh, even to Jahaz they have uttered their voice, from Zoar even to Horonaim, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for the waters of Nimrim will also become desolate.” (web:Jer.48.34). Yahweh's own voice returns explicitly, וְהִשְׁבַּתִּ֥י לְמוֹאָ֖ב נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה מַעֲלֶ֣ה בָמָ֔ה וּמַקְטִ֖יר לֵאלֹהָֽיו (oshb:Jer.48.35, byte), matching “Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab,” says Yahweh, “him who offers in the high place, and him who burns incense to his gods.” (web:Jer.48.35) — a fresh first-person pronouncement attributed by name, without displacing the surrounding lament register, and the heart-like-flutes figure follows, עַל כֵּ֞ן לִבִּ֤י לְמוֹאָב֙ כַּחֲלִלִ֣ים יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְלִבִּי֙ אֶל אַנְשֵׁ֣י קִֽיר חֶ֔רֶשׂ כַּחֲלִילִ֖ים יֶהֱמֶ֑ה עַל כֵּ֛ן יִתְרַ֥ת עָשָׂ֖ה אָבָֽדוּ (oshb:Jer.48.36, byte), matching “Therefore my heart sounds for Moab like flutes, and my heart sounds like flutes for the men of Kir Heres. Therefore the abundance that he has gotten has perished.” (web:Jer.48.36). Mourning rites are catalogued next, כִּ֤י כָל רֹאשׁ֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְכָל זָקָ֖ן גְּרֻעָ֑ה עַ֤ל כָּל יָדַ֨יִם֙ גְּדֻדֹ֔ת וְעַל מָתְנַ֖יִם שָֽׂק (oshb:Jer.48.37, byte), matching “For every head is bald, and every beard clipped. There are cuttings on all the hands, and sackcloth on the waist.” (web:Jer.48.37), and the housetops' own lamentation, עַ֣ל כָּל גַּגּ֥וֹת מוֹאָ֛ב וּבִרְחֹבֹתֶ֖יהָ כֻּלֹּ֣ה מִסְפֵּ֑ד כִּֽי שָׁבַ֣רְתִּי אֶת מוֹאָ֗ב כִּכְלִ֛י אֵֽין חֵ֥פֶץ בּ֖וֹ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.38, byte), matching “On all the housetops of Moab, and in its streets, there is lamentation everywhere; for I have broken Moab like a vessel in which no one delights,” says Yahweh.” (web:Jer.48.38) — this verse too closes on neum-YHWH, but no fresh tier-1 onset follows at the next verse, so it corroborates rather than closes a unit here. The lament reaches its own climax in a string of exclamations, אֵ֥יךְ חַ֨תָּה֙ הֵילִ֔ילוּ אֵ֛יךְ הִפְנָה עֹ֥רֶף מוֹאָ֖ב בּ֑וֹשׁ וְהָיָ֥ה מוֹאָ֛ב לִשְׂחֹ֥ק וְלִמְחִתָּ֖ה לְכָל סְבִיבָֽיו (oshb:Jer.48.39, byte), matching “How it is broken down! How they wail! How Moab has turned the back with shame! So will Moab become a derision and a terror to all who are around him.” (web:Jer.48.39). A setumah closes oshb:Jer.48.39 in the parashah inventory (WLC, single-witness; tier-3 weak corroboration under the Prophets addendum). That mark corroborates the row's own close immediately before the fresh divine-speech formula that opens the next verse, כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֥ה כַנֶּ֖שֶׁר יִדְאֶ֑ה וּפָרַ֥שׂ כְּנָפָ֖יו אֶל מוֹאָֽב (oshb:Jer.48.40, byte), matching “For Yahweh says: “Behold, he will fly as an eagle, and will spread out his wings against Moab.” (web:Jer.48.40).
